content: Nicotine skin patches are prescribed to assist individuals in quitting smoking. They deliver a controlled amount of nicotine to the body, which helps alleviate withdrawal symptoms that occur when smoking cessation begins. Nicotine patches are applied directly to the skin. They should be used once daily, ideally at the same time each day. These patches are available in different strengths and are used for varying durations, depending on the specific instructions provided by your doctor or pharmacist. It is crucial to follow the directions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Use the patches exactly as directed, without exceeding or reducing the prescribed dosage or frequency. To apply the patch, select a clean, dry, and hairless area of skin, such as the upper chest, upper arm, or hip, as specified in the package instructions. Avoid applying the patch to irritated, oily, scarred, or broken skin. Remove the patch from its packaging, peel off the protective strip, and immediately place the sticky side onto your skin. Press the patch firmly in place with the palm of your hand for about 10 seconds, ensuring it adheres securely, especially around the edges. After application, wash your hands with water only. If the patch falls off or becomes loose, replace it with a new one. The patch should be worn continuously for 16 to 24 hours, depending on the specific instructions provided with your nicotine patch. It can be worn while showering or bathing. When removing the patch, fold it in half with the sticky sides together and dispose of it properly. Apply the next patch to a different area of skin to prevent irritation. Never wear two patches simultaneously. After the first two weeks of use, your doctor may recommend switching to a lower-strength patch to gradually reduce nicotine withdrawal symptoms. Nicotine patches are typically used for a duration of 6 to 20 weeks, depending on the specific instructions provided. Before using nicotine skin patches, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to adhesive tape or any medications. Additionally, provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially acetaminophen (Tylenol), caffeine, diuretics (water pills), imipramine (Tofranil), insulin, medications for high blood pressure, oxazepam (Serax), pentazocine (Talwin, Talwin NX, Talacen), propoxyphene (Darvon, E-Lor), propranolol (Inderal), theophylline (Theo-Dur), and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of heart attack, irregular heart rate, angina (chest pain), ulcers, uncontrolled high blood pressure, overactive thyroid, pheochromocytoma, or any skin conditions or disorders. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using nicotine patches, contact your doctor immediately, as nicotine and nicotine patches may harm the fetus. Do not smoke cigarettes or use other nicotine products while using nicotine patches, as this can lead to nicotine overdose. If you forget to apply a patch, do so as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply two patches to make up for a missed dose. Nicotine patches may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: dizziness, headache, upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea, or redness or swelling at the patch site. If you experience severe side effects such as a severe rash or swelling, seizures, abnormal heartbeat or rhythm, or difficulty breathing, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store nicotine patches in their original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep them at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unused patches by folding them with the sticky sides together and keeping them out of reach of children or pets. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using nicotine patches. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
